body:
TWO MORE MERGED AND THE LAST DRIVE PR DIRECTED. Eight tonight: BUG-1275, BUG-1285, BUG-1290, BUG-1294, BUG-1295, BUG-1299, STORY-1352, TASK-1296.

#1992 (BUG-1275) MERGED. The fix is argued from measurement rather than intuition, which is what I most expected to be a guess: 1200s sits above the measured 705-second p95 of the last 97 CI runs, with the command that produced it in the comment. The real fix is the re-arm, not the number — an in-flight required check is itself liveness, so a long check that simply took a while stops being indistinguishable from a dead one. Raising the window alone would have moved the cliff. I verified the ceiling is still evaluated BEFORE the idle timer, because a re-arm is exactly the change that creates an unbounded wait by accident. The env-var docs were updated in the same change with both rows rewritten rather than renumbered.

#1987 (STORY-1352) MERGED. I checked the enforcement rather than the prose, since a versioned interface with no mechanism is a wish. Both halves run in CI: the fixtures are compared against the LIVE manifest, and the base-ref comparison demands a minor bump for an added field and a major for a removed one. The unit tests include that a major bump PERMITS a breaking change, which is the case that stops the rule being merely restrictive.

I merged it over an informational Windows red after checking both failures by name: the lock test (BUG-1303) and the pull-rebase test whose fix sits unmerged in #1977. Neither introduced there. That is the same judgement I corrected myself on earlier, and it is also live evidence for your feedback loop — #1977 holds a PROVEN fix for one of those two, so every branch's cross-platform run keeps failing on something we have already fixed and not landed. That makes the matrix look worse than it is and buries the genuinely open defect.

One follow-up recorded on that spec, not blocked on: the drift guard runs under a path filter that excludes docs, and the contract's own fixtures live in docs. Any code change triggers it, but a fixtures-only change would not run the guard that validates fixtures. One line closes it.

#1989 (STORY-1353) — RED, AND IT IS NOT A BROKEN TEST. Requeued with direction rather than a brief.

  rework_needs_attention_spec_becomes_pickable_queue_head FAILED
  "rework would advance Needs Attention → In Progress, which needs advisor authority;
   dispatch authority alone cannot dispose a spec"

The implementation classifies NeedsAttention → InProgress as a disposition. That blocks the exact workflow this spec was written to unblock, and the spec's own description is the argument: "roughly twenty-five reviewer-finding-to-rework-brief cycles. Every one of them needed the advisor prefix, and not one of them approved anything." Those twenty-five ARE this transition. The change would ship having moved the boundary without moving the case it exists for.

The distinction I directed: a disposition decides WHETHER work proceeds — Approved, Rejected, Superseded, Deferred — and stays advisor-only. Resuming work that was already approved and then shelved is not that decision; it was made at approval and the shelve did not reverse it. So rework moving a shelved spec back into play is dispatch, and the test asserting it is right. I told the lane explicitly not to weaken or delete that test, and that if it finds itself editing the assertions the boundary is still wrong.

WHY I HELD RATHER THAN MERGING WITH A FOLLOW-UP, and it is bigger than one red test. Tonight's recovery arrangement is that a shelved spec gets requeued promptly, and BUG-1291 and STORY-1218 both depend on something moving shelved work back into play without a human in the loop. If that transition needs advisor authority, every recovery from every shelve routes through a seat that only acts when something wakes it, and substrate-first recovery becomes unreachable by construction.

GATE STATE: nothing at my gate is now waiting on me. Eleven holds, every one waiting on a change I have specified: 1972 fail-open, 1977 split, 1979 third reader, 1981 two guards, 1982 Option type, 1983 is_running, 1988 content check, 1989 authority boundary, 1991 someone other than me, 1996 three lines. Nine of those are one small change each.
